level.title: Define Phase
level.description: Learn to clearly define the problem, scope, and goals of a Six Sigma project.

lessons.title: Project Charter & Problem Statement
lessons.content_md:
# Project Charter & Problem Statement

The **Project Charter** is the foundational document of any Six Sigma project. It answers: *What are we fixing, why, and for whom?*

## Elements of a Project Charter

### 1. Problem Statement
A clear, quantifiable description of the issue:
- **Bad**: "Our data collection process has problems."
- **Good**: "15% of household survey forms in Q2 2024 contained data entry errors in income fields, causing 3-week delays in tabulation."

### 2. Goal Statement
What success looks like, using SMART criteria:
- **Specific**: Reduce data entry errors in income fields
- **Measurable**: From 15% to below 2%
- **Achievable**: Similar divisions achieved 1.5%
- **Relevant**: Directly impacts data quality
- **Time-bound**: Within 6 months

### 3. Scope
- **In scope**: Data entry process for PLFS household surveys
- **Out of scope**: Field enumeration methodology, sampling design

### 4. Team
- Champion: Director (ESD)
- Black Belt: Deputy Director
- Green Belts: 2 Assistant Directors
- Team Members: 4 SSOs

### 5. Timeline
Milestone-based DMAIC schedule with review gates.

lessons.title: Voice of Customer (VOC) & SIPOC
lessons.content_md:
# Voice of Customer (VOC) & SIPOC

## Voice of Customer

VOC captures what stakeholders need from a process. In government:

| Stakeholder | Need | CTQ (Critical to Quality) |
|---|---|---|
| Parliament | Timely GDP estimates | Published within 60 days of quarter end |
| Researchers | Clean microdata | <1% missing values in key variables |
| States | District-level data | All 780+ districts covered |
| Citizens | Transparent methodology | Documentation publicly available |

### How to Capture VOC
1. **Surveys**: Structured feedback from data users
2. **Complaints**: Analyze recurring issues
3. **Benchmarking**: Compare with international NSOs
4. **Interviews**: Direct conversations with stakeholders

## SIPOC Diagram

SIPOC maps the high-level process:

| S (Suppliers) | I (Inputs) | P (Process) | O (Outputs) | C (Customers) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field enumerators | Survey schedules | Data collection → Entry → Validation → Tabulation | Statistical tables, reports | Parliament, researchers, states |
| IT division | Software, servers | | Microdata files | International agencies (UN, World Bank) |

## Critical-to-Quality (CTQ) Tree

Breaks down broad needs into measurable requirements:

```
Need: Accurate GDP Estimate
├── Driver: Reliable source data
│   ├── CTQ: <2% revision between advance and final estimate
│   └── CTQ: 95% response rate from large enterprises
└── Driver: Timely publication
    ├── CTQ: Advance estimate by Jan 7
    └── CTQ: Final estimate within 11 months
```
